name: Astrid unvalidated restaked-token withdrawal
summary: AstridProtocol.withdraw accepted any caller-supplied restaked-token contract without requiring it to match a whitelisted stakedTokens entry. Fake tokens reported attacker-chosen stakedTokenAddress and scaledBalanceToBalance values, so withdrawal processing recorded the protocol's real stETH, rETH and cbETH reserves as claimable and claim transferred them to the attacker.

loss.notes: The receipt shows 64.176037513415148812 stETH, 39.165842900855519099 rETH and 20.000407064566313222 cbETH leaving Astrid. The attack contract liquidated all three inside its constructor and forwarded exactly 127.797499079942863577 ETH to the attacker EOA. At the nearest pre-incident DefiLlama ETH price of 1,789.94 USD, those exact realised proceeds are worth 228,749.85550315292923101538 USD. Gas is not deducted and no recovery is netted.

ageReset.description: The proxy's second and last pre-exploit Upgraded event selected AstridProtocol implementation 0x4d5b4b9ccf52bbcfe7b71b3038d8577293779e0c.

sources.note: The anchor is the attacker's nonce-0 top-level creation of exploit contract 0xb2e855411f67378c08f47401eacff37461e16188, so it is the earliest possible defect-executing transaction for that EOA. The constructor deploys three fake restaked-token contracts and performs withdraw(address,uint256), withdrawalRequestsByUserLength(address) and claim(uint256) against Astrid proxy 0xbaa87546cf87b5de1b0b52353a86792d40b8ba70. Every frame delegates to 0x4d5b4b9ccf52bbcfe7b71b3038d8577293779e0c. Its verified AstridProtocol source checks only that the caller-supplied restaked-token address contains code and that its balance and allowance are sufficient; it never binds that address to the whitelisted stakedTokens mapping. _processWithdrawals then trusts stakedTokenAddress() and scaledBalanceToBalance() on that same contract, and claim again trusts stakedTokenAddress() before paying the recorded amount. In the trace, the fake tokens return stETH, rETH and cbETH respectively and report each entire Astrid balance as claimable; the proxy transfers 64.176037513415148812 stETH, 39.165842900855519099 rETH and 20.000407064566313222 cbETH. Their in-transaction liquidation returns exactly 127.797499079942863577 ETH to the attacker EOA, worth 228,749.85550315292923101538 USD at 1,789.94 USD per ETH. Code history: the ERC1967 proxy was top-level created by 0xcbf060349b8f56ce80bd559e3999aad55128d1aa in source-3 at block 18291584:117. It emitted exactly two Upgraded events before exploitation. The second and last is source-5 at block 18413660:102, log 196, selecting 0x4d5b4b9ccf52bbcfe7b71b3038d8577293779e0c in topic1. The proxy's EIP-1967 slot still holds that address immediately before exploitation, and the implementation runtime hashes to 0x43b608f21d83711b7d8c0e8a4070b23720ea50f74ac8ef3a1b8e87b0ba9e8178 at activation and pre-exploit. processWithdrawalsOnWithdraw was set true at block 18292606 shortly after proxy deployment and was already true before the last upgrade; it stayed true through exploitation, so no later causal parameter change supersedes the code activation. The measured age is 417,204 seconds (4.83 days).

limitations: The exact figure is the attacker's realised ETH proceeds rather than a gross incident-time mark of the stETH, rETH and cbETH victim basket.
